initiative.title: Custom metrics and repository settings
initiative.summary: Use private file metrics and diagnostics in Srcly views, with repeatable repository settings. Imports and policy first; explicit commands follow.
initiative.next_action: Review the shape and authorize implementation when ready; begin with the three-file import proof.

sources.anchor: Coworker wants their own metrics processed; repository limits, thresholds, settings and defaults
Completed Pro response: research-report.md, implementation-plan.md, recommendations.md; all read on 2026-10-23.
Direct source checks against aea1015: fixed IDs, direct getters, static compare table, path-only evidence requests, current color/bar shortcuts

claims.statement: Developers can use Srcly visualization with their own metrics and checks.
Repository settings can define useful limits, thresholds, settings and defaults.
Import, overlay and plugin mechanisms remain alternatives to research.
Preserve measured zero, unknown values, and source association in custom views and reports.
Complete research and a new planned initiative before application implementation.

shape.appetite: Three milestones for useful native imports and repo settings; later adapter and explicit command slices; conditional snapshot proof.
shape.problem: Private metrics cannot reach all Srcly consumers, and repository limits/defaults have no shared policy resolver.
shape.recommended_shape: Native file results with typed measurements and diagnostics, small custom-value accessors, per-scan effective context, one declarative repo policy. Explicit producers feed the same boundary later.
success_moves: Use a deterministic three-file bundle before implementing an analyzer or command runner.
Keep custom observations beside fixed built-ins; adapt consumers through small shared accessors.
Install values and reactive definitions together per scan to prevent cross-repo leakage.
Separate source, artifact and interpretation invalidation; prove reload with AST reuse.
Defer profiles, CI gates and portable comparison beyond the first release.
Test actual descendant termination before exposing explicit custom execution.

first_proof.question: Can a new metric ID and separate diagnostic reach views and reports without losing zero or unknown semantics?
first_proof.artifact: Temporary three-file Git fixture, native bundle and minimal srcly.toml; one browser pass and raw report exports
first_proof.decision_rule: Continue only when a=2, b=0, c=unknown, folder subtotal=2 with 2/3 measured, and diagnostic opens a.ts:2 under the correct scan catalog.

shape.simpler_counterproposal: Import diagnostics only through the existing findings runner. Rejected as the complete solution: it cannot carry arbitrary numeric units, aggregation or IDs. Retained as reuse for diagnostic presentation.

repository_snapshot.worktree_status: Clean application baseline; research/docs only on codex/extensibility-config-research
deployment_surfaces: Local FastAPI server and bundled SolidJS client; no deployment needed for proof

milestones.title: One imported metric and line diagnostic reach views and reports
milestones.outcome: Custom file values and separate diagnostic appear across UI and reports with minimal repo config.
milestones.proof: Temporary fixture a=2, b=0, c=unknown; subtotal 2 and 2/3 measured; line 2 navigation; checks-off fresh/cache test; repo switch parity.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Opt-in native import works for plain tracked file-local inputs; built-ins remain usable.
milestones.rollback: Remove import or use explicit no-config/no-results/checks-off bypass.

milestones.title: Imports remain useful after edits and reloads
milestones.outcome: Dirty/non-Git file imports, conflicts, source status and reload are dependable.
milestones.proof: Source edit removes current line marks without changing zero or denominator; artifact-only reload reuses AST; conflicting/malformed imports stay visible.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: File-local inputs work outside clean Git; uncertain repo-dependent computations remain inspectable only.
milestones.rollback: Bypass results; preserve old data only as stale.

milestones.title: Repository settings give repeatable interpretation
milestones.outcome: One selected policy defines defaults, exclusions, selected limits, colors, risk bands and named quadrant cutoffs.
milestones.proof: Root/package/worktree fixture proves discovery and precedence; interpretation changes retain raw values; exclusions rebuild the tree; threshold equality checks.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: First useful release: dependable imports and repeatable repo policy without new profiles or gates.
milestones.rollback: Explicit no-config and reset personal choices; invalid policy errors clearly.

milestones.title: One existing diagnostics format works without its tool
milestones.outcome: A real saved SARIF or ESLint output feeds existing native results presentation.
milestones.proof: Captured positive/empty/failed outputs retain producer, rules, lines and unknown coverage; no tool executes.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: One named external format alongside native bundles.

milestones.title: A developer explicitly runs their own check
milestones.outcome: A deliberate CLI/UI action runs a configured local command and accepts validated output.
milestones.proof: Fixture executable tests literal argv, accepted codes, invalid output, timeout and child cancellation; real producer smoke follows.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Explicit execution on tested platforms; imports work without executables.

milestones.title: Evaluate portable result comparison
milestones.outcome: A conditional proof determines whether small saved-context comparison is worth adding.
milestones.proof: Two saved fixture contexts compare without producers; policy-only edit stays distinct; missing head evidence is not zero.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Either verified dependency-free snapshot compare or an explicit deferred extension; ordinary scans remain usable.
milestones.rollback: Omit snapshot route; reject unsupported artifact versions directly.
